content_partner: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa
creator: New Zealand National Airways Corporation
Weeks Field Ltd.
results.description:
This pictorially-rich poster for NAC (National Airways Corporation) conveys the complexity of air travel routes and tourism in New Zealand in the 1950s. The border cleverly comprises images of tourist activities, ideal landscapes, Maori culture, flora and fauna, showing how New Zealand was presented as a tourist destination to both domestic and international audiences.
NAC was New Zealand's government-owned domestic airline established under the New Zealand National Airways Act in 1945. In 1947, NAC began flying to the Pacific between Auckland and Norfolk Island, Nadi, Tonga, Western Samoa and Aitutaki–Rarotonga. NAC withdrew from most Pacific services five years later in favour of Tasman Empire Airways Ltd (TEAL), the long-distance imperial carrier owned by New Zealand, Australia and the United Kingdom. 
NAC was taken over by Air New Zealand in 1978.

results.description:
This poster by the Wellington branch of the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament protests against French power and nuclear testing in the Pacific.
Between 1966 and 1996, France carried out about 190 nuclear tests at Moruroa and Fangataufa atolls in French Polynesia. These caused reef damage, landslides, subsidence, radioactive emissions, and fish poisoning.
The poster features the logo for the Nuclear Free and Independent Pacific Movement. The movement was formed in 1980 to widen the struggle against nuclear testing in the Pacific to independence from colonial powers.

content_partner: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa
creator: Arthur Thompson
results.description:
In this poster Arthur Thompson (1915 – 1997) plays on Tahiti’s reputation as a mysterious and exotic destination, complete with beautiful women. Tahiti was the final stop on TEAL’s Coral Route - a romantic island hop from Auckland to Papeete. The name ‘Coral Route’ came from a TEAL staff competition. Head steward Eric Mullane’s winning entry was inspired by the beauty of coral islands and of Pacific people’s song-filled (‘choral’) receptions for their visitors. At Papeete, disembarking passengers were greeted with the dance ‘Soirée de TEAL’.
In the 1950s, Thompson worked for TEAL (Tasman Empire Airways Limited), the forerunner of Air New Zealand. Exotic, colourful designs enticed travellers onto TEAL’s flights to glamorous destinations across the Pacific.
Thompson was a commercial artist who worked in New Zealand and Britain. He studied at the Elam School of Fine Arts and in the 1960s had a successful career as a costume and set designer for film and television.

results.description:
This poster advertises a march to take place in Wellington, New Zealand, on 4 August 1990, calling for independence and peace for the areas of the Pacific suffering from foreign rule and nuclear testing. The poster states:
'Over two hundred nuclear tests have been carried out in the Pacific since 1946. Over half of these were by France, with the rest by the United States and Britain. As a result of these tests many people, such as the people of Bikini atoll, Enewetak and Kwajalein, have been dispossessed of their land, and their health has been affected. Radioactive fallout, including that from the USSR and China, will continue to fall from the sky for years to come. Where foreign rule continues, as in New Caledonia, Tahiti and Micronesia, the abuse of the people and their land for military purposes continues. The rule and the weapons of all outside powers must be removed from the Pacific.'

creator: Arthur Thompson
results.description:
This poster by Arthur Thompson (1915 – 1997) conjures up the tropical delights of Fiji, the first stop on TEAL’s island-hopping Coral Route. Fiji was one of the airline’s most popular destinations. The romance of the Pacific and TEAL’s stylish flying boats proved to be an irresistible combination for wealthy international tourists.
In the 1950s, Thompson worked for TEAL (Tasman Empire Airways Limited), the forerunner of Air New Zealand. Exotic, colourful designs enticed travellers onto TEAL’s flights to glamorous destinations across the Pacific.
Thompson was a commercial artist who worked in New Zealand and Britain. He studied at the Elam School of Fine Arts and in the 1960s had a successful career as a costume and set designer for film and television.

creator: Trace Hodgson
results.description:
This poster calls for people to join a demonstration against the visit of French Prime Minister Michel Rocard to Wellington, New Zealand on 29 April 1991.
The protest was against French nuclear testing in the Pacific. Between 1966 and 1996, France carried out about 190 nuclear tests at Moruroa and Fangataufa atolls in French Polynesia. These caused reef damage, landslides, subsidence, radioactive emissions, and fish poisoning.
Community spirit
The poster is interesting for its sense of humour and community spirit - not only was there to be a deadly serious demonstration - live entertainment was provided for the crowds turning up to demonstrate.
